sections.1.heading: What invoicing software for coaches should do
sections.1.body:
Good **invoicing software for coaches** has to handle two very different kinds of client. Individuals often pay for themselves, by the session or in packages. Companies pay for coaching for their staff, and their finance teams expect invoices that show what was delivered, to whom and when.

The second kind is where billing gets complicated. One company might sponsor three leaders, each with their own programme, plus stakeholder interviews, assessment debriefs and a check-in with HR. If all of that becomes one line saying "Coaching services, March", it tends to come back with questions.

Paidlyo approaches this from the time side:

- **Each paying client** is a client in Paidlyo, whether a company or an individual.
- **Each coachee or programme** is a project, so a company sponsoring three leaders has three projects.
- **Each kind of work** is a task: sessions, preparation, stakeholder interviews, reports.
- **Rates are set per project or task,** so a session and prep time can be billed differently.
- **At month end,** invoices are built from unbilled hours in one click.

This page is for coaches who bill companies and individuals for their time. It isn't for therapists or counsellors who bill insurers or handle clinical records, which need specialist practice software.
sections.2.heading: Sessions, prep and follow-up
sections.2.body:
Coaching hours are more than the time on the call. Preparation, reading assessment results, writing session notes and following up by email all take time, and many coaches don't bill any of it because they never measured it.

Start by tracking everything for a month, even work you don't plan to bill. Use a few simple tasks:

| Task | What goes in it | Billed? |
|---|---|---|
| Coaching session | Time in the session itself | Yes |
| Preparation | Reviewing notes and materials before a session | Depends on contract |
| Stakeholder interviews | Conversations with managers or peers | Usually yes |
| Reports and debriefs | Assessment reports, written summaries | Usually yes |
| Admin and scheduling | Emails, booking, invoicing | No |

Mark each entry billable or not. At the end of the month, the hours report shows how much unbilled time sits behind each paid hour. If every one-hour session takes another 45 minutes of preparation, you know your real hourly rate is much lower than your session rate.

That number helps in two ways. You can raise your session price, or you can agree with corporate clients that preparation and reports are billed separately, as their own lines on the invoice.
sections.2.callout: Put your billing rules for prep and reports in the coaching agreement. Clients rarely object to time they agreed to in writing.
sections.3.heading: Packages and programmes
sections.3.body:
Many coaches sell packages: 6 sessions over three months, or a 12-session leadership programme. Paidlyo invoices are built from tracked time, so the way you use it depends on how the package is paid.

**Billed as you go.** If the client pays for sessions as they're delivered, track each session and invoice monthly from unbilled hours. Set a **project budget** for the package hours so you can see how many are left.

**Paid upfront.** If the client pays for the whole package in advance, issue that invoice from your accounting tool, then use Paidlyo to track the sessions against a budget. You'll know exactly when the package is used up and can talk to the client about renewal before the last session, not after it.

Here's how a budget helps with a 12-session programme of 90-minute sessions:

| Point in the programme | Hours used | Hours left |
|---|---|---|
| After session 4 | 6 | 12 |
| After session 8 | 12 | 6 |
| After session 10 | 15 | 3 |

At session 10, it's time for the renewal conversation. Without a budget, that moment often passes unnoticed.

Paidlyo doesn't create recurring or subscription invoices, and it doesn't take payments upfront, so it suits coaches who bill sessions as they're delivered better than those selling memberships.
sections.4.heading: Billing corporate sponsors clearly
sections.4.body:
Corporate coaching often has three parties: the coach, the coachee and the company paying. The invoice goes to the company, and it needs to make sense to someone in finance who wasn't in the room.

A few habits make corporate invoices easy to approve:

- **One project per coachee,** so you can group the invoice by project and each leader appears separately.
- **Session lines with hours,** rather than one total, so the client can match them to their own records.
- **Separate lines for non-session work,** such as stakeholder interviews and reports.
- **The company's purchase order or reference** in the project name, if they ask for one.
- **The client's currency,** set once per client, if the company is abroad.

Invoices carry your logo and can include tax where you're registered and a discount if you've agreed one. The client receives a private link and opens the invoice without an account, then saves a PDF for their approval process.

Confidentiality matters in coaching. Invoices show sessions and hours, not what was discussed, so keep task names neutral: "Coaching session" rather than anything that hints at content.

When the client pays, record the payment. The outstanding invoices report shows which sponsors are late and by how long.

faq.1.question: Can I bill a company for several coachees on one invoice?
faq.1.answer: Yes. Make each coachee a project under the company, then group the invoice by project.
faq.2.question: Does Paidlyo handle coaching packages?
faq.2.answer: Set a project budget for the package hours and watch it as you track sessions. Upfront package invoices are best issued from your accounting tool.
faq.3.question: Can clients book sessions or pay by card?
faq.3.answer: No. Paidlyo has no booking or card payments. Clients pay by your agreed method, and you record it.
faq.4.question: Is Paidlyo suitable for therapists?
faq.4.answer: No. Therapy and counselling practices that bill insurers or keep clinical records need specialist practice software.
